prompt.context: Our client, InsureCo, is a large, multi-national insurance provider with revenues of over $25B in 2009. The tightening of credit markets and an economic downturn has caused their profitability to drop significantly from 10% to 5% in the most recent year. As a result, InsureCo has decided to evaluate their business portfolio and divest portions of their business to raise capital and refocus on their core General Insurance business. Their goal is to raise over $3B in capital through the sale of various business units. Management has already identified two potential candidates for divestiture from its Life Insurance and Property and Casualty divisions: (1) LifeLine Asia — an Asian-based life insurance business with $250MM in annual revenues; and (2) All-World Property and Casualty — a US-based P&C insurance business with $100MM in annual revenues. Deloitte Consulting has been engaged to identify and recommend the most viable business unit candidates for divestiture and to assist in the operational separation of business units from InsureCo.
prompt.question: 1. What would you estimate as the potential sales price for each company? Please use available data to support your argument. 2. Which company would you advise InsureCo to divest? 3. What are some of the other key factors that InsureCo should consider when assessing which units to divest?

clarifying_info.q: Are there any financial benchmarks or deal comparables available?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — the interviewer provides a data sheet with industry deal multiples and segment/geography trends.

clarifying_info.q: Is InsureCo looking to divest both units or just one?
clarifying_info.a: They are considering divesting one of the two identified units, in addition to several other businesses across the company.

clarifying_info.q: What is the net income for each of the two candidate business units?
clarifying_info.a: No explicit net income figures are provided in the prompt; the candidate must work from available revenue data and industry multiples from the data sheet.

exhibits.title: Data Sheet
exhibits.shows: Industry deal multiples (P/E) for the Life Insurance and P&C segments over time, and an overview of deal activity by segment and geography (North America vs. Asia trends).
exhibits.data: Life Insurance P/E multiple (recent): ~10x; P&C P/E multiple (recent): ~20x; LifeLine Asia implied earnings: ~$20MM; All-World P&C implied earnings: ~$12MM; Life segment trend: declining; P&C segment trend: increasing; North America geographic trend: declining; Asia geographic trend: increasing

framework: Valuation: Estimate sales price for each unit using comparable deal multiples (P/E approach)
Strategic fit: Assess which divestiture better aligns with InsureCo's goal of refocusing on core General Insurance
Qualitative factors: People/culture, geographic reach, revenue interdependencies, potential buyers, and separation complexity

questions.prompt: 1. What would you estimate as the potential sales price for each company?
questions.guidance: A good answer applies available P/E multiples to each unit's implied earnings. A better answer notes the directional trend in multiples (Life declining, P&C rising) and uses the most recent multiples. A great answer also weighs how segment trends (Life declining, P&C growing) and geography trends (North America declining, Asia growing) affect long-term value and buyer appetite.

math.setup: Use P/E multiple × net earnings to estimate sale price. Derive implied earnings from the data sheet; apply recent (most favorable/current) multiples.
steps: LifeLine Asia implied earnings: ~$20MM; recent Life P/E multiple: 10x → estimated price = $20MM × 10 = $200MM
All-World P&C implied earnings: ~$12MM; recent P&C P/E multiple: 20x → estimated price = $12MM × 20 = $240MM
math.answer: LifeLine Asia ≈ $200MM; All-World P&C ≈ $240MM. Based on recent multiples, All-World commands a higher estimated sale price despite lower revenues.

questions.prompt: 2. Which company would you advise InsureCo to divest?
questions.guidance: Either answer can be correct if well-supported. If recommending LifeLine Asia: higher average historical multiple could yield a higher price; Asia is a growing market commanding a premium; Life is a declining segment InsureCo may want to exit. If recommending All-World P&C: recent deal multiples favor P&C, yielding a higher current price; P&C sector is growing and buyers will pay a premium; more straightforward to price and exit.

questions.prompt: 3. What are the other key factors InsureCo should consider when assessing which units to divest?
questions.guidance: A good answer is logically structured across multiple business dimensions. A great answer adds shared infrastructure considerations.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key factors InsureCo should consider when assessing which business units to divest?

categories.name: People and Culture
ideas: Impact on employee morale and retention when high-quality assets are sold
Grooming pipeline: executives being developed in divested units must be retained or transitioned

categories.name: Geographic Reach and Overlap
ideas: Identify geographic overlap between divested unit and remaining business
Evaluate whether exiting a geography weakens InsureCo's global competitive position
Consider whether the buyer will compete in InsureCo's remaining markets

categories.name: Revenue Interdependencies
ideas: Cross-sell impact: if the divested unit distributes other InsureCo products, revenue will be lost
Assess downstream revenue risk from lost referrals or distribution channels
Evaluate contractual obligations between divested and retained units

categories.name: Potential Buyers and Deal Execution
ideas: Identify prospective strategic and financial buyers
Assess regulatory and antitrust considerations for each buyer
Consider IPO/spin-off path: adds legal and regulatory complexity
Evaluate whether competitive bidders exist to maximize sale price

categories.name: Shared Infrastructure and Separation Complexity
ideas: IT systems: divested units often rely on parent's technology infrastructure
Finance, HR, and legal shared services must be carved out
Sales and marketing platforms and distribution networks
Estimate time and cost to achieve full operational separation (Day One readiness)
Risk of business disruption during the transition period

recommendation: Based on recent deal multiples, divest All-World Property and Casualty for an estimated ~$240MM; alternatively, divest LifeLine Asia if strategic priority is exiting the declining Life segment while capturing Asian market premium
The recommended unit should align with InsureCo's goal to refocus on core General Insurance and maximize capital raised toward the $3B target
risks: Divesting a growing-geography asset (LifeLine Asia) foregoes future upside in the Asian insurance market
P&C sector growth means retaining All-World could also be strategically valuable — opportunity cost of divesting a rising segment
Revenue cross-sell disruption if divested units distribute other InsureCo products
Separation complexity and cost could erode net proceeds from either divestiture
next_steps: Conduct detailed financial due diligence on both units to refine earnings and valuation
Map all shared infrastructure dependencies to estimate separation cost and timeline
Run a structured buyer outreach process to test market appetite and pricing
Develop Day One readiness plan and separation blueprint for the selected unit
Assess remaining portfolio for additional divestiture candidates to close the gap toward $3B target
